### Observed differences

- The activities involved did not appear or disappear: A20, A21, A22, A30, A31 and A36 occur in essentially every trace in both windows (200 of 200 traces each), so the difference lies in sequencing, not in participation. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- In the earlier window, A30, A31 and A36 each ran before A21 and before A22 in 100 in 100 traces; in the later window this is reversed, with A21 and A22 each running before A30, A31 and A36 in about 99 in 100 traces, while the activities still always co-occur. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- In the earlier window, A20 was followed by A30 (about 40 in 100 outgoing transitions), A31 (about 33) or A36 (about 28), and A22 followed four positions after A20; in the later window A20 is followed directly by A22 in about 99 in 100 cases (distance of 1 position). [DIR001, LAG001]
- In the earlier window, A21 was always followed immediately by A25; in the later window A21 is followed by A30 (about 36 in 100), A31 (about 33) or A36 (about 31), and A25 is reached only about four positions after A21. [DIR002, LAG004]
- The exit of the A30/A31/A36 group changed: earlier, each of the three led to A22 in roughly 29–38 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (otherwise to another group member); in the later window they lead to A25 at similar rates (about 31–36 in 100) and almost never to A22 (about 0.5 in 100). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Event positions moved accordingly: A21 and A22 now occur earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.62 to 0.53 and 0.47 to 0.38), while A30, A31 and A36 occur later (about 0.41 to 0.59). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Four LAG items on pairs around the group (A20–A31, A20–A36, A31–A22, A36–A22) rest on only about 2 after-window observations each and carry little weight on their own. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering of the case sequence around the three-activity block A30, A31, A36: in the earlier window the block ran between A20 and A22 (A20 handed over to one of the three, the group circulated internally, and its last member led to A22, while A21 led straight to A25), whereas in the later window the block runs between A21 and A25 (A20 leads directly to A22, A21 hands over to one of the three, and the group's last member leads to A25). Equivalently, A22 and A21 now execute ahead of the group instead of behind it, with the group's internal circulation preserved. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

The order reversal is shown directly by the relation indicators — deterministic flips from 100 in 100 to about 99 in 100, with both activities co-occurring in every trace in both windows — and is corroborated by the successor changes at A20 and A21, the gap changes (A20→A22 from four positions to one; A21→A25 from one to four) and the consistent position shifts. Participation is unchanged, so this is not a shift in how often existing paths are taken. The 22 qualifying items compare with roughly 0.42 expected from random re-splits of an unchanged process, and every item's difference exceeds those seen in about 995 of 1,000 reference re-splits, so sampling variation cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

Limitations: POS and LAG are based on event positions rather than clock time, so on their own they would not establish movement — the relational evidence carries the hypothesis. The evidence shows that the relative order of the group and of A21/A22 flipped together with the successor changes, but it cannot distinguish whether the group moved later or the A21/A22 segment moved earlier (competing readings of the same reordering), and it says nothing about the segment between A22 and A21 or about parts of the process outside these activities; the four low-support LAG items cannot clarify the group's internal order in the later window. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Other differences: none — every qualifying item describes the same reordering of A20, A21, A22, A25 and the A30/A31/A36 group. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
